title: display: block, inline, inline-block, none
learningObjectives: Explain display: block, inline, inline-block, none and apply the layout behaviour correctly.

understand.concept: The display property controls an element's outer and inner display behaviour. block boxes participate as block-level boxes; inline boxes flow within line boxes; inline-block participates inline while accepting box dimensions; none removes the element and its descendants from layout and the accessibility tree in common cases.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing display changes layout behaviour, not the semantic meaning of the HTML element. display:none is not a visual-only hiding technique because hidden content is generally unavailable to assistive technology.
understand.analogy: Display is the layout role an element takes in its surrounding flow, not a replacement for choosing the correct HTML element.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; the browser uses formal formatting, containing-block, and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The block sample starts on a new line, inline stays within text flow, and inline-block accepts a width while sitting inline.

examples.explanation: The block sample starts on a new line, inline stays within text flow, and inline-block accepts a width while sitting inline.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered page demonstrating the relevant CSS layout behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create four labelled examples and compare block, inline, inline-block, and none. Note which item disappears from layout.
practise.independentTask: Build a small layout that demonstrates this behaviour. Test long content, keyboard navigation, and narrow viewports.
hints: Inspect computed styles and layout overlays.
Change one property at a time.
Keep semantic HTML independent from visual display choices.

questions.prompt: Which display value removes an element from layout?
questions.explanation: display:none removes the element from the layout tree.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to understand a layout behaviour?
options: Inspect the browser result and change one rule at a time
Assume every element uses the same containing block
Add z-index values without checking stacking contexts
questions.answer: Inspect the browser result and change one rule at a time
questions.explanation: A controlled experiment plus developer tools reveals the browser's actual layout behaviour.
